classification.classification_note: The observed fault is a 1-byte stack out-of-bounds write into `tmp[SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH]` inside `mosquitto__hex2bin()`. Source-level root cause is that the leading-zero loop writes one output byte per leading `"00"` pair before the later BIGNUM-size guard runs, and it never checks that those in-loop writes stay within `bin_max_len`.

bug_description.original_source: sample metadata issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / live staged vulnerable source checkout in gt-arvo_55948-workspace
bug_description.normalized: The staged 547-byte config witness begins with the parser-visible prefix ` tls_engine_kpass_sha1       00000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000ire_ocksp ` before the first embedded NUL byte. `config__read_file_core()` tokenizes that prefix as option `tls_engine_kpass_sha1`, `conf__parse_string()` trims and duplicates the remainder into `kpass_sha`, and `config__read_file_core()` passes that string to `mosquitto__hex2bin_sha1()`. `mosquitto__hex2bin_sha1()` allocates stack scratch buffer `tmp[SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH]` and calls `mosquitto__hex2bin(hex, tmp, SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH)`, so the destination extent is exactly 20 bytes. Because the parsed string starts with 59 `0` characters, `mosquitto__hex2bin()` sees 29 consecutive leading `"00"` pairs and writes one zero byte to `tmp` for each pair before `BN_hex2bn()` or the later `BN_num_bytes(bn) + leading_zero > bin_max_len` guard runs. The 21st in-loop `bin[start++] = 0` store lands at `tmp[20]`, one byte past the 20-byte stack object that AddressSanitizer reports in `mosquitto__hex2bin_sha1`. The fix adds an early `if(leading_zero >= bin_max_len){ return 0; }` guard before each leading-zero store, preventing the overflow.

source.description: First project parser statement that turns the attacker-controlled config line into vulnerability-relevant state by extracting the option token and leaving `saveptr` pointing at the remainder later materialized as `kpass_sha`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 547-byte config file. Before the first embedded NUL at byte 98, its parser-visible prefix is ` tls_engine_kpass_sha1       00000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000ire_ocksp `. This tokenization yields `token == "tls_engine_kpass_sha1"` and a remainder whose trimmed value begins with 59 `0` characters.
source.note: Source. The vulnerability-relevant parser state starts here: the same attacker-controlled line simultaneously selects the `tls_engine_kpass_sha1` option arm and exposes the long value that will later be scanned for leading `"00"` pairs.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. On the 21st matching leading-zero pair, this store writes one byte past the 20-byte stack buffer `tmp` provided by `mosquitto__hex2bin_sha1()`.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `WRITE of size 1` at this exact line and identifies `tmp` in `mosquitto__hex2bin_sha1` line 157 as the overflowed stack object `[32,52)`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The leading-zero loop writes one output byte for every matching `"00"` pair but never checks that those in-loop writes stay within `bin_max_len`, so more than 20 leading zero bytes overflow the fixed SHA1 scratch buffer before the later BIGNUM-size guard executes.
root_cause.note: The fix adds the missing early guard inside this loop. On the staged witness there are 29 qualifying pairs, so after 20 earlier writes `start` has already advanced to 20 and the 21st pair still executes the same store.

tainted_value_origin.description: This duplicates the trimmed remainder of the `tls_engine_kpass_sha1` config line into heap string `kpass_sha`, the exact attacker-controlled string later scanned by `mosquitto__hex2bin()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Immediately before the copy, `*token` is the trimmed string `00000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000ire_ocksp `, which begins with 59 `0` characters, i.e. 29 full leading `"00"` pairs.
tainted_value_origin.note: Only the parser-visible prefix before the file's first embedded NUL reaches this string logic, because earlier `strlen(*buf)` truncates the C-string view of the line at that NUL.

parser_admitted.description: Option dispatch admits the parsed line to the vulnerable TLS SHA1 path. The saved runtime log shows `REQUIRE_LISTENER_OR_DEFAULT_LISTENER(token)` created a default listener here, so the config is not rejected for lacking an earlier `listener` line.

evidence_limitations: The exact staged source inspected in Stage 02 is the live ARVO container checkout `gt-arvo_55948-workspace:/src/mosquitto` at commit `be688e883b734fc421e1dc1931a349b4d9afea49`, not a plain source tree stored under the result directory. The staged checkout's line map matches the saved AddressSanitizer trace and patch hunk.

Stage 01 reproduced only the vulnerable AddressSanitizer crash. No fixed-build execution was performed in this Stage 02 session, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` is kept false even though `patch.diff` clearly adds the missing in-loop bound check.

Runtime disambiguation is disabled in `run_flags.json`, so no extra instrumentation was permitted. The exact parser-visible prefix, embedded-NUL truncation, and count of 29 leading `"00"` pairs are therefore derived statically from the staged `poc` bytes and the inspected vulnerable source.

fine_trace.note: Source. On the first parser-visible config line, this yields `token == "tls_engine_kpass_sha1"` and leaves `saveptr` pointing at the long value substring. That value's trimmed prefix begins with 59 `0` characters before the nonzero tail `ire_ocksp`.

The parsed option name selects the TLS SHA1 parser path. The saved run log confirms that `REQUIRE_LISTENER_OR_DEFAULT_LISTENER(token)` created a default listener here, so processing continues even though the witness does not define a listener first.

The remainder of the same config line is trimmed and duplicated into `kpass_sha`. For the staged witness, `kpass_sha` begins with 59 `0` characters, then the ASCII tail `ire_ocksp`, so the later conversion loop will encounter 29 full leading `"00"` pairs.
The attacker-controlled string is now consumed by the SHA1-specific hex decoder. No earlier parser check constrains the number of leading zero bytes to the 20-byte SHA1 destination.

fine_trace.code:
unsigned char *sha, tmp[SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH];
if(mosquitto__hex2bin(hex, tmp, SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH) != SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH){
fine_trace.note: The wrapper creates stack scratch buffer `tmp[20]` and calls `mosquitto__hex2bin()` with `bin_max_len == SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH == 20`. AddressSanitizer later identifies this exact local as the overflowed object `[32,52)`.

Scanning the staged `kpass_sha`, this loop sees 29 consecutive matching leading `"00"` pairs because the string begins with 59 zero characters. The thirtieth two-byte window is `"0i"`, which finally breaks the match.

Root cause step. This loop body has no in-loop guard such as the fix's `leading_zero >= bin_max_len` before storing into `bin`. After the first 20 matching pairs, `start` has already advanced to 20, but the 21st pair still takes this branch. The later `if(BN_num_bytes(bn) + leading_zero > bin_max_len)` check is below the loop and cannot stop these writes.

Sink. On the 21st matching pair, `bin` still aliases `tmp` and `start == 20`, so this stores one byte at `tmp[20]`, one past the 20-byte stack object. The saved AddressSanitizer report records `WRITE of size 1` at this exact line.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The saved patch inserts `if(leading_zero >= bin_max_len){ return 0; }` immediately before the leading-zero store in `mosquitto__hex2bin()`, which is the missing guard identified by the source trace.
